claims.assertion: The driver drove 18.0 km against an optimal 15.1 km (+2.9 km, +19%) and took 30.1 min against a 20.6 min estimate, so the trip was demonstrably longer than the shortest and most direct route the driver owes the rider.

The GPS track contains exactly one off-route segment, 12:27–12:35, in which 4.90 km were driven where the optimal route covers 2.75 km, adding 2.16 km and reaching up to 722 m off the optimal route; that segment is an unexcused detour under RD-1.

The only rider message before the segment is '随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间' (12:25), which is a general route authorisation to pick whichever way is faster — it reaches route choice only, not a driver's own stop or loop; under RD-5 a general authorisation does not cover a deviation that no rider message asked for.

The rider's general authorisation of the fastest route does not make the driven route an exempt one: no traffic incident is recorded near the route during the trip window, and RD-4(a) requires a DataMall incident located on the replaced stretch of the optimal route before a reroute is excused.

The driver's post-trip statement that the rider 'said any faster way was fine' is a claim, not consent, and in any case it is no wider than the chat message itself — a general route authorisation, not approval of the specific 12:27–12:35 loop.

This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so the extra 2.16 km of the unexcused segment directly entered the fare; RD-2 therefore awards the rider the extra distance at this trip's own per-km rate, and the fare record shows that rate is $1.4098/km (distance fare $25.39 ÷ 18.01 km).

The driver has no prior upheld dispute and the rider has none either (both 0 upheld in 90 days), so RD-6's precondition of a repeated breach is not met and the rider does not ask for a flag_account action; the request is confined to the fare refund.
